about.title: South Lake Tahoe Wrongful Death Claims
about.longDescription: Losing a family member in a traffic collision is one of the hardest things a person can go through, and it's made harder when it happens on roads you drive every day — Lake Tahoe Boulevard, Emerald Bay Road, Pioneer Trail, or Ski Run Boulevard. El Dorado County's public crash records show dozens of injury collisions each year in this area, and while recent reporting shows no recorded traffic deaths, fatal crashes do happen on Tahoe's mountain and lakeside corridors, especially where tourist traffic mixes with local commuters during peak weekend hours. If your family has lost a spouse, parent, or child in a crash near South Lake Tahoe, an independent attorney in our network can review what happened, explain your legal options under California's wrongful death statute, and help you understand what comes next. LawProactive doesn't charge you to connect with that attorney, and there's no obligation to move forward. You deserve time to grieve, not a legal maze to figure out alone.

whyChoose.title: What Families in South Lake Tahoe Should Know

items.title: Strict Time Limits Apply
items.desc: California generally allows two years from the date of death to file a wrongful death claim, though claims against a government entity involving a public road may require faster action. Waiting too long can permanently close the door on your family's case.

items.title: Only Certain Family Members Can File
items.desc: California law limits who has standing to bring a wrongful death claim, typically starting with a surviving spouse, domestic partner, or children, then extending to other dependents or heirs in specific situations. An attorney can clarify who in your family qualifies before any claim moves forward.

items.title: Recoverable Losses Go Beyond the Bills
items.desc: California wrongful death law allows families to seek compensation for funeral costs and lost financial support, but also for the loss of love, companionship, and guidance a person provided. An attorney can help make sure both the financial and personal losses are accounted for.

items.question: Who in my family is allowed to file a wrongful death claim in California?
items.answer: California law generally gives priority to a surviving spouse, registered domestic partner, or children to bring the claim. If none of those relatives exist, certain other dependents or heirs may have standing instead. An independent attorney can look at your family's specific situation and confirm who qualifies.

items.question: How long do we have to file after losing a loved one in South Lake Tahoe?
items.answer: California generally sets a two-year deadline from the date of death to file a wrongful death lawsuit. If the crash involved a government-maintained road, like sections of Lake Tahoe Boulevard or Pioneer Trail, the timeline to act may be much shorter. It's worth speaking with an attorney as soon as you're able.

items.question: Does a wrongful death claim depend on criminal charges being filed?
items.answer: No. A wrongful death claim is a separate civil action from any criminal case that may or may not be pursued against a driver. Even if no charges are filed, or charges are still pending, your family can still pursue a civil claim for damages. These two processes move on independent tracks under California law.
